tpms.when: 2017 (first-generation Evoque, sensors in each wheel; no reset button)
steps: Set all four tires, and a full-size spare if you carry one, to the cold pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker.
There is no reset button. The system reads each tire's sensor by itself, so correct pressures are what clear the light.

If you carry a heavy load, use the instrument panel menu to switch the tire pressure monitoring load setting from Normal (light) load to Heavy load, and set the tires to the higher loaded pressures on the sticker.
If a wheel or tire was removed or swapped, drive for at least 15 minutes so the system can relearn the sensor positions.
After driving above about 16 mph, a low-pressure warning should go out within about 5 minutes.
If the light is still on after the pressures are right and you have driven, have the system checked by a qualified shop.
tpms.note: If the light flashes for about 75 seconds and then stays on, the system cannot read one or more sensors (for example winter wheels with plain rubber valves). Setting pressures will not clear that.

notes: From the Range Rover Evoque owner's handbook marked for the 2017 model year onward. The handbook says the service message countdown is reset on completion of a service but gives no driver steps, so no oil reset is listed here.
